title: Supply Chain Logistics Network
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D supply chain logistics network simulation using Three.js (CDN). The scene models a network of factories, warehouses, and retail stores connected by transport routes.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 60, 80) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0.4 intensity) and a directional light from (30, 50, 20) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
- Render a large ground plane (200x200) with a subtle grid texture (dark gray, 0x2a2a2a) to represent a map.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Network Nodes (3 tiers)
1. FACTORIES (3 nodes): Red cylinders (radius 3, height 6) placed at (-60,3,0), (-60,3,30), (-60,3,-30). Each factory produces goods at a configurable rate (default 5 units/sec). Each has a max inventory of 200.
2. WAREHOUSES (3 nodes): Blue boxes (4x4x4) placed at (0,2,20), (0,2,0), (0,2,-20). Each warehouse stores goods with max capacity 300. Warehouses act as intermediaries.
3. RETAIL STORES (4 nodes): Green spheres (radius 2.5) placed at (60,2.5,30), (60,2.5,10), (60,2.5,-10), (60,2.5,-30). Each store consumes goods at a configurable rate (default 3 units/sec). If inventory reaches 0, the store sphere turns yellow (stockout).

## Transport Routes
- Draw lines (THREE.Line with dashed material) connecting each factory to each warehouse, and each warehouse to each retail store. Total 9+12=21 routes.
- Animate small white spheres (radius 0.5) traveling along active routes to represent shipments. Shipments carry a quantity (default 10 units) and travel at speed 15 units/sec.
- A shipment is dispatched automatically when a source node inventory >= 10 and a connected destination node has capacity.

## Simulation Physics & Conservation
- TOTAL GOODS CONSERVATION: The total goods in the system (sum of all node inventories + all in-transit shipment quantities) must remain consistent. Factories add goods to the system (production), stores remove goods (consumption). Track totalProduced and totalConsumed. Enforce: totalProduced - totalConsumed === allInventories + allInTransit (within epsilon 0.5).
- Inventories must never go below 0 or above their max capacity.
- Shipment positions must be interpolated linearly between source and destination.

## User Interactions
- KEYBOARD 'P': Toggle pause/resume simulation.
- KEYBOARD 'R': Reset entire simulation to initial state (all inventories to 50, clear all shipments, reset counters).
- KEYBOARD '+' / '-': Increase/decrease global simulation speed multiplier (0.5x to 3.0x, step 0.5).
- KEYBOARD '1','2','3': Select factory 1, 2, or 3. Selected node gets a yellow wireframe outline.
- KEYBOARD 'U': Undo last speed change (maintain a history stack of up to 10 speed changes).
- CLICK on any node (raycasting): Select that node and display its details in the HUD.
- DOM BUTTON 'Add Surge': Instantly add 50 units to all factory inventories (respecting max capacity).
- DOM BUTTON 'Toggle Route': Disable/enable the route between the currently selected node and its first connected neighbor. Disabled routes turn red and stop dispatching shipments.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left panel showing: simulation time (seconds, 1 decimal), speed multiplier, paused status.
- Top-right panel showing: totalProduced, totalConsumed, totalInTransit, conservation check (OK/VIOLATION).
- Bottom panel showing selected node info: name, type, current inventory, max capacity, connections count.
- Two buttons: 'Add Surge' and 'Toggle Route' styled with dark background and white text.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- paused (boolean)
- simTime (number, seconds elapsed)
- speedMultiplier (number)
- speedHistory (array of previous speed values)
- factories (array of {id, inventory, maxInventory, productionRate})
- warehouses (array of {id, inventory, maxInventory})
- stores (array of {id, inventory, maxInventory, consumptionRate, stockout})
- shipments (array of {id, from, to, quantity, progress}) where progress is 0.0 to 1.0
- totalProduced (number)
- totalConsumed (number)
- totalInTransit (number)
- conservationValid (boolean) — true if totalProduced - totalConsumed is within epsilon of sum of all inventories + totalInTransit
- selectedNodeId (string|null)
- disabledRoutes (array of {from, to} objects)
- nodeCount (number, total nodes = 10)
- routeCount (number, total routes = 21)
- activeRouteCount (number, routes not disabled)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame.
physics_constraints: Conservation law: totalProduced - totalConsumed must equal sum of all node inventories plus totalInTransit within epsilon 0.5. Inventories clamped to [0, maxCapacity]. Shipment progress in [0,1]. Speed multiplier in [0.5, 3.0].
